specification.problem: Quantized density classification with a Quantum Particle Automaton (QPA): for a binary input of length 5, evolve a single-particle state with a unitary U and decide majority 0 or 1 by the probability mass on either side of a boundary partition of position basis states. U and the partition are found by a genetic algorithm.
specification.reconstruction_scope: Smallest construction: n=5 binary input encoded as the initial particle amplitude on a 5-site line, evolution by an unspecified unitary U(theta), a boundary partition of basis states into two sets, and a GA fitness defined as classification accuracy. Not covered: the actual GA design details, the specific unitary form, the parameter theta's exact role, the found solutions, scaling to arbitrary n, and the QPA definition from the cited source.

symbols.meaning: initial particle state encoding x (encoding is assumed)
unitary evolution operator found by GA
parameter of U that sets the evolution speed (small theta: small mass, fast evolution)
boundary partition of position basis states into the two decision sides
symbols.domain: disjoint subsets of {0,...,4} whose union is {0,...,4}

symbols.meaning: probability that the measured particle lies in B_b
GA fitness: classification accuracy over inputs

equations.label: Evolution
equations.description: Unitary evolution of the particle state for t steps
equations.abstract_quote: the QPA needed a unitary operator to carry out the QPA evolution
equations.justification: The abstract says a unitary operator carries out the evolution; the power-t form assumes a discrete-time repeated application.

equations.label: Side probability
equations.description: Born-rule probability that the particle collapses to a basis state in side B_b of the partition
equations.abstract_quote: when the particle was measured, it was more likely to collapse to the basis states that were on the correct side of the boundary partition
equations.justification: Collapse to basis states on a side of a partition implies Born-rule probabilities summed over that side.

equations.label: Decision rule
equations.description: Classify as majority 0 or 1 according to the more probable side
equations.justification: A natural decision rule consistent with 'more likely to collapse' to the correct side; the exact rule is not given.
assumptions: B_b is associated with majority-b label

equations.label: GA fitness
equations.description: Fraction of the 32 inputs classified correctly; the GA searches for U and the partition maximizing this
equations.justification: Plausible fitness for the described GA search; the actual fitness is not stated.

equations.label: Majority label
equations.description: Majority density label for odd length 5 (no ties)
equations.justification: The standard definition of density classification; length 5 is odd so it is well defined.

registers.name: position
registers.role: particle position on the 5-site lattice; qubit embedding is assumed

specification.initial_state: Not specified in the abstract; assumed |psi_0(x)> encodes the 5-bit input x as a function of site (e.g. amplitudes weighted by the bits), normalized.

steps.description: Encode input x into the initial particle state (encoding assumed).
Apply the GA-found unitary U for t steps.
Measure the position and compute side probabilities for the partition.
Decide majority label from the more probable side.
Outer classical loop: GA optimizes U and the partition using the fitness.

specification.measurement: Measure the particle in the position basis and assign the outcome to side B_0 or B_1 of the boundary partition.
specification.classical_postprocessing: Aggregate outcomes into side probabilities or a majority vote over shots; GA fitness evaluation and selection over candidate (U, partition) pairs.
assumptions: Input encoding, lattice geometry, number of steps t, and boundary structure are not given in the abstract and are assumed.
The functional form of U(theta) is not given; U is treated as a general unitary.
The GA's operators, population, and fitness are not given; the fitness is an assumed accuracy.
missing_information: QPA definition and the exact form of U including the role of theta
Input encoding into the initial state
